summary_paragraph: A woman with advanced AIDS (CD4 41, off HAART) and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis via a right femoral tunneled catheter was admitted with purulent femoral catheter tunnel infection, leg pain/swelling, chills, and hypotension after dialysis. The infected femoral catheter was removed and she was treated empirically with vancomycin dosed with dialysis (cefepime was started initially then stopped due to low suspicion for gram-negative infection); blood cultures remained negative and she had no fevers. Ultrasound of the right thigh showed soft tissue edema without a drainable abscess. Interventional radiology ultimately placed a new tunneled hemodialysis catheter via the left femoral vein after an initial unsuccessful attempt; during placement, contrast suggested a possible IVC thrombus, so heparin was started briefly but discontinued after CT venography showed a patent IVC without thrombosis. She experienced intermittent dialysis-associated hypotension and a transient EKG finding of bigeminy without symptoms; review of prior EKGs noted past atrial fibrillation in the setting of sepsis, and aspirin was increased to 325 mg daily. Throat pain improved with empiric nystatin for suspected oral candidiasis. Depression was addressed with psychiatry and social work planning, and she was discharged home with services to continue dialysis and opportunistic infection prophylaxis with outpatient follow-up.
problems: Other and unspecified infection due to central venous catheter
